text.p: Cargolux recent decision to buy an additional Boeing 747-400 freighter , making a total of five, is a pointer to the type of aircraft the European cargo carrier needs, Pierre Wesner, Cargolux' vice-president, Europe/Africa/Middle East, told Reuters.

"Investing in two additional 747-400F, as opposed to one, as was initially planned, is an indication of the strong technical and economic argument which the type of aircraft represents. The long-term renewal policy of our fleet will probably mean one day we'll be operating the 400 exclusively with the phase-out of the 747-200F."

"The truth is the majority of our cargo routes are more suited to the operation of 400s than 200s. The two new aircraft will give us considerably greater scope to realise productivity gains and keep unit costs in check while also providing a marketing edge in facilitating the development of long-haul routes which of course is where the best yields can be obtained," he added.
Cargolux had not yet decided whether it would maintain its four-strong 747-200F fleet in its entirety in the light of the 747-400F fleet rising to five, Wesner said.
"It's probably a little exaggerated to see us a total of nine aircraft in service but the recomposition of the fleet is still under discussion."
The 400 can carry up to 124 tonnes of cargo per flight over more than 4,400 miles with the lowest operating costs per ton-mile, Cargolux said in a previous statement.

Cargolux 400 destinations from Luxembourg include Komatsu, Hong Kong, Tapei, Johannesburg, Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Mexico City and Sao Paulo. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
